text: FCVariable is a data type. E.g. DataType[z, FCVariable] = True.
If we want to introduce constants c1 and c2, the naive way doesn’t lead to the desired result
SPD[c1 p1 + c2 p2, q] // ExpandScalarProduct
The solution is to declare c1 and c2 as FCVariable so that FeynCalc can distinguish them from the 4-momenta
DataType[c1, FCVariable] = True; DataType[c2, FCVariable] = True;
SPD[c1 p1 + c2 p2, q] // ExpandScalarProduct
This works also for propagator denominators and matrices
FCI[SFAD[{q + c1 p1, m}]] // StandardForm (*FeynAmpDenominator[StandardPropagatorDenominator[c1 Momentum[p1, D] + Momentum[q, D], 0, -m, {1, 1}]]*)
GAD[\[Mu]] . (GSD[c1 p] + m) . GAD[\[Nu]] // FCI // StandardForm (*DiracGamma[LorentzIndex[\[Mu], D], D] . (m + c1 DiracGamma[Momentum[p, D], D]) . DiracGamma[LorentzIndex[\[Nu], D], D]*)
CSI[i] . CSIS[c1 p] . CSI[j] // FCI // StandardForm (*PauliSigma[CartesianIndex[i]] . (c1 PauliSigma[CartesianMomentum[p]]) . PauliSigma[CartesianIndex[j]]*)
DataType[c1, FCVariable] = False DataType[c2, FCVariable] = False
